prompt: For بِسْمِ, what are the visible pieces and why is a host-only gloss 'name' unsafe?
expected_answer: The token is بِـ (preposition) + host noun ٱسْمِ; the hover must preserve the bā' ('in the name of'), because a host-only 'name' drops the prepositional relation that is part of the token.
accepted_variants: bā' preposition + host اسم; 'in the name of', not 'name'
forbidden_answers: the whole token is one noun

prompt: For أَعْطَيْنَاكَ, name the pieces and the safe gloss, and why bare 'gave' fails.
expected_answer: Verb host أَعْطَيْـ + subject marker نا (we) + object pronoun كَ (you); the gloss is 'We gave you'. Bare 'gave' fails because it drops the subject 'we' and the object 'you' that the attached pieces carry.
accepted_variants: verb + نا subject + كَ object; 'We gave you'
'We gave you'; bare 'gave' drops subject and object
forbidden_answers: the كَ object pronoun can be omitted

concept: tanwīn-alif is not the pronoun نا
prompt: For قُرْءَانًا, why must you not split a final نا as an attached pronoun?
expected_answer: The final ـًا is tanwīn fatḥ on a carrier alif (nunation, an indefinite marker), not the attached pronoun نا. Do not split it as a pronoun; the token is one indefinite noun.
accepted_variants: ـًا is tanwīn on a carrier alif, not the pronoun نا
no clitic split; it is nunation, not 'us'
forbidden_answers: the نا is an attached pronoun 'us'
split off نا as a suffix
the alif is a separate word

prompt: For وَٱلْعَصْرِ at the start of a sūrah, why can 'and' be wrong, and what must be settled first?
expected_answer: The clause-initial وَ may be an oath particle ('by'), not the coordinating 'and'; the frame must be settled before glossing. With the oath frame the token is 'by (the) time', and the article ٱل and host ٱلْعَصْر keep their roles.
accepted_variants: oath waw 'by', not 'and', once the oath frame is set
settle oath vs conjunction before glossing وَٱلْعَصْرِ
forbidden_answers: the article can vanish into the noun

concept: active-participle plural, not the entry verb
prompt: For ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ, why is an entry gloss 'to succeed' unsafe, and what does the token contribute?
expected_answer: The token is ٱل + an active-participle plural host; it contributes 'the successful ones', not the entry infinitive 'to succeed'. A derived noun is glossed as a noun, and the plural ending must be visible.
accepted_variants: 'the successful ones'; reject the verb 'to succeed'
active-participle plural, glossed as a noun with the plural ending shown
forbidden_answers: the entry infinitive is the gloss
